svg.title: Figure C-0-2. Follow one hazard: HE-01.2 to SG-01 and its requirements
svg.desc: A vertical chain of six steps. 1, the item element (WP-C-01): the EPS torque command over CAN, 0x2E4 STEERING_LKA (torque, steer request). 2, the operating situation (WP-C-02, WP-C-08): OS-01/OS-02 highway, adjacent traffic or barrier, 90–110 km/h, ODD speed 0 – 110 km/h (68 mph), not above the posted limit, a supervising driver. 3, the hazardous event HE-01.2 (WP-C-03): Lateral departure into an adjacent vehicle or barrier; S3, E4, C2 ⚠, ASIL C, ASIL D if AOU-01/02 are not verified. 4, the safety goal SG-01, ASIL C ⚠ (D if AOU-01/02 fail): The item shall not cause lateral motion of the vehicle that exceeds what the driver can control, including any steering actuation while the item is not engaged 5, the requirements (WP-C-04): FSR-01.01 torque magnitude limit, ASIL C, allocated to E-03, now partial; FSR-01.02 torque rate limit, ASIL C, allocated to E-03, now implemented without rationale; FSR-01.03 torque tracks the measured EPS torque, ASIL C, allocated to E-03, now implemented; FSR-01.13 EPS keeps LKA torque overpowerable, ASIL — (ext.), allocated to EXT-EPS, now unverified. 6, where it is shown: the 3D scene he-01-2-hardover-adjacent of the gallery, contact with the adjacent car at +2.21 s, 10 km/h, with a still of its 3D view.
svg.text: One thread through the documents: from the steering command on the CAN
bus to the requirements that limit it, and the scene that shows HE-01.2.
0x2E4 STEERING_LKA (torque, steer request), sent on IF-01,
Highway at up to 110 km/h, supervising driver
OS-01/OS-02 highway, adjacent traffic or barrier, 90–110 km/h.
ODD speed: 0 – 110 km/h (68 mph), not above the posted limit.
Controllability C2 rests on a supervising driver.
HE-01.2: steering hard-over into the adjacent lane
Lateral departure into an adjacent vehicle or barrier (H-01
ASIL D if AOU-01/02 are not verified
SG-01 · ASIL C ⚠ (D if AOU-01/02 fail)
The item shall not cause lateral motion of the vehicle that exceeds
what the driver can control, including any steering actuation while
Safe state: LKA torque request zero, steer request bit cleared; driver
informed. FTTI ≤ 0.5 s (preliminary). HE-01.2 is its governing event.
torque rate limit; now: implemented without rationale
torque tracks the measured EPS torque; now: implemented
EPS keeps LKA torque overpowerable; now: unverified
E-03: Safety envelope: opendbc safety (Toyota mode) and the panda
firmware paths it relies on, on the STM32H7
Outcome in the scene: contact with the adjacent car at +2.21 s, 10
km/h. Synthetic: a picture, no evidence credit.

g.text: Terms: AOU-nn assumption of use (WP-C-01 §7); an R suffix marks the FSC's
refined version · ASIL Automotive Safety Integrity Level, A (lowest) to D
(highest), from ISO 26262 · C0–C3 controllability class C0 (controllable in
general) to C3 (difficult or uncontrollable) · CAN controller area network: the
vehicle's data bus · E-nn element of the item (WP-C-01 §3.1), E-01…E-06 · E0–E4
exposure class E0 (incredible) to E4 (high probability) · EPS electric power
steering · EXT-nn external element credited only through an assumption of use
(EXT-EPS, EXT-PCM, EXT-CLU) · FSR-nn functional safety requirement (FSC) · FTTI
fault-tolerant time interval: fault to hazard, the time a safety mechanism has ·
H-nn hazard (HARA) · HE-nn hazardous event (HARA) · IF-nn interface of the item
(WP-C-01 §3.4) · LKA lane keeping assist · ODD operational design domain: where
the system is meant to work · OS-nn operational situation (HARA §3) · S0–S3
severity class S0 (no injuries) to S3 (life-threatening) · SG-nn safety goal
(HARA §6) · WP-nn work product, e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its area (M
management, C concept, S system, H hardware, W software, V validation, P
processes, A analyses, O operation, K safety case)
